# Natural Kind Analysis Quality Checklist

> After each natural kind analysis, check each item. A fully checked list indicates a high-quality analysis.

---

## Kind Theory Identification

- [ ] **Complete kind claims catalog**: Has every natural kind claim in the argument been cataloged (KC1...KCn) with kind term, domain, classification claim, kind theory hint, and structural role?
- [ ] **Lexical evidence cited**: Does the theory diagnosis cite specific kind-related vocabulary from the argument (essence, cluster, homeostasis, construction, lineage, causal role)?
- [ ] **Five diagnostic tests applied**: Have all five tests (lexical, criteria, uniqueness, realism, modal) been applied and their results documented?
- [ ] **Alternative theories considered**: Has the report evaluated whether an alternative kind theory would better fit the argument (and argued for rejecting or noting ambiguity)?
- [ ] **Secondary/inconsistent commitments flagged**: If the argument mixes kind theory commitments (e.g., essentialist language but HPC functional roles), has this been detected and flagged?

## Essentialist/Non-Essentialist Classification

- [ ] **Essence specification check**: If essentialism is diagnosed, has the report checked whether the argument specifies the essence and whether the specification is adequate (with counterexample testing)?
- [ ] **Stereotype-essence gap flagged**: Has the report identified any conflation of the stereotype (surface identification) with the essence (underlying nature)?
- [ ] **Twin Earth test applicability**: Where applicable, has the argument's reliance on Twin Earth-style reasoning been evaluated?
- [ ] **Modal force calibration**: Has the report verified that the argument's modal claims (necessary, nomic, contingent) match what the kind theory licenses?

## HPC Analysis

- [ ] **Property cluster described**: If HPC is diagnosed, has the report checked that the property cluster is described (which properties co-occur)?
- [ ] **Homeostatic mechanism identified**: Has the report verified that the argument identifies the causal mechanism maintaining the cluster, not merely listing co-occurring properties?
- [ ] **Mechanism specification gap flagged**: If the argument claims HPC without specifying the homeostatic mechanism, has this gap been flagged?
- [ ] **Projectibility qualified**: Has the report assessed whether the argument acknowledges the qualified (rather than deductive) nature of HPC projectibility?

## Cross-Domain Consistency

- [ ] **Domain inventory complete**: Are all domains in which kind claims appear inventoried, with domain-specific adequacy assessed?
- [ ] **Uniformity check performed**: Has the report checked whether the argument treats kinds uniformly across domains, and whether uniformity is appropriate?
- [ ] **Domain-specific guidelines applied**: Have the domain-specific adequacy guidelines (chemistry, biology, psychology, social kinds, medicine, everyday objects) been applied?
- [ ] **Theory-switching detected**: If the argument switches between kind theories across domains, has this been flagged as intentional (pluralism) or unacknowledged (inconsistency)?
- [ ] **Biological species sensitivity**: If biological species are classified, has the report engaged the species problem and flagged species essentialism as a minority position?

## Conventionalism Assessment

- [ ] **Social kind boundary conditions applied**: If the argument concerns social kinds, has the analysis engaged looping effects (Hacking), normative entanglement, and naturalizing critiques?
- [ ] **Conventions or purposes specified**: Under conventionalism or practical kinds, has the report checked whether the argument specifies the conventions or purposes grounding the classification?
- [ ] **Normative leap detection**: Has any unargued inference from descriptive kind membership to normative status been flagged?

## Report Quality

- [ ] **Inference evaluation complete**: Has every kind-based inference in the argument been evaluated (inferential basis, justification, modal calibration, normative leap, circularity)?
- [ ] **Alternatives section substantive**: Does the Alternative Kind Theories section genuinely evaluate how the argument fares under different theories, rather than merely listing alternatives?
- [ ] **Dialectical implications assessed**: Has the report identified whether the argument's conclusions depend on its choice of kind theory, and whether opponents can challenge by adopting a different theory?
- [ ] **Pluralism awareness maintained**: Has the report avoided assuming kind monism is mandatory, evaluating pluralism (if present) on its own terms?
- [ ] **Evidence traceable**: Is every diagnostic claim traceable to specific textual evidence from the argument rather than being asserted without support?
